word_for_word: वैराग्येण विना ज्ञानं न च भक्तिरतः स्फुटम्। वैराग्योपस्कृतं ज्ञानमीशः पञ्चदशेऽदिशत्।।1।।पूर्वाध्यायान्तेमां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते इत्यादिना परमेश्वरमेकान्तभक्त्या भजतस्तत्प्रसादलब्धज्ञानेन ब्रह्मभावो भवतीत्युक्तम्? नचैकान्तभक्तिर्ज्ञानं वाऽविरक्तस्य संभवतीति वैराग्यपूर्वकं ज्ञानमुपदेष्टुकामः प्रथमं तावत्सार्धश्लोकाभ्यां संसारस्वरूपं वृक्षरूपकालंकारेण वर्णयन्श्रीभगवानुवाच -- ऊर्ध्वमूलमिति। ऊर्ध्वमुत्तमः क्षराक्षराभ्यामुत्कृष्टः पुरुषोत्तमो मूलं यस्य तम्। अध इति ततोऽर्वाचीनाः कार्योपाधयो हिरण्यगर्भादयो गृह्यन्ते? ते तु शाखा इव शाखा यस्य तम्। विनश्वरत्वेन श्वः प्रभातपर्यन्तमपि न स्थास्यतीति विश्वासानर्हत्वादश्वत्थं प्राहुः। प्रवाहरूपेणाविच्छेदादव्ययं च प्राहुःऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः इत्याद्याः श्रुतयः। छन्दांसि वेदाः यस्य पर्णानि? धर्माधर्मप्रतिपादनद्वारेण छायास्थानीयैः कर्मफलैः संसारवृक्षस्य सर्वजीवाश्रयणीयत्वापादनात्पर्णस्थानीया वेदाः। यस्तमेवंभूतमश्वत्थं वेद स एव वेदार्थवित् संसारप्रपञ्चवृक्षस्य मूलमीश्वरः श्रीनारायणः? ब्रह्मादयस्तदंशाः शाखास्थानीयाः? स च संसारवृक्षो विनश्वरः प्रवाहरूपेण नित्यश्च वेदोक्तैः कर्मभिः सेव्यतामापादितश्चेत्येतावानेव हि वेदार्थः। अतएव विद्वान्वेदविदिति स्तूयते।

Knowledge and devotion are impossible without dispassion; therefore in the fifteenth the Lord teaches knowledge furnished with dispassion. At the end of the previous chapter it was said that one who worships the Supreme Lord with exclusive, unwavering bhakti obtains knowledge through His grace and thereby reaches the state of Brahman. Since neither exclusive devotion nor knowledge is possible for one without dispassion, He first describes saṃsāra by the metaphor of a tree in one and a half verses. Its root is above: the Supreme Person, superior to both perishable and imperishable. ‘Below’ refers to later effects and limiting adjuncts such as Hiraṇyagarbha, which are like its branches. It is called aśvattha because, being perishable, it cannot be trusted to remain even until tomorrow morning; yet it is called imperishable because its stream continues without interruption, as scriptures say ‘This eternal aśvattha has its root above and branches below.’ The Vedic metres, the Vedas, are its leaves, because by teaching dharma and adharma they make the saṃsāra-tree a refuge for all beings through karmic fruits that function like shade. Whoever knows such an aśvattha truly knows the meaning of the Veda: Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Lord, is the root of the tree of worldly manifestation; Brahmā and others are branches as portions of Him; the saṃsāra-tree is perishable yet continuous like a stream, and Vedic actions make it something to be resorted to. This is the substance of the Veda, so such a knower is praised as a knower of the Veda.

किंच -- अधश्चेति। हिरण्यगर्भादयः कार्योपाधयो जीवाः शाखास्थानीयत्वेनोक्ताः? तेषु च ये दुष्कृतिनस्तेऽधः पश्वादियोनिषु प्रसृताः विस्तरं गताः? सुकृतिनश्चोर्ध्वं देवादियोनिषु प्रसृतास्तस्य संसारवृक्षस्य शाखाः। किंच गुणैः सत्त्वादिवृत्तिभिर्जलसेचनैरिव यथायथं प्रवृद्धाः वृद्धिं प्राप्ताः। किंच विषया रूपादयः प्रवालाः पल्लवस्थानीया यासां ताः? प्रशाखास्थानीयाभिरिन्द्रियवृत्तिभिः संयुक्तत्वात्। किंच अधश्च चशब्दादूर्ध्वं च मूलानि अनुसंततानि विरूढानि। मुख्यं मूलं ईश्वर एक एव। इमानि त्ववान्तरमूलानि तत्तद्भोगवासनालक्षणानि। तेषां कार्यमाह। मनुष्यलोके कर्मानुबन्धीनि कर्म एवानुबन्धि अनन्तरभावि येषां तानि ऊर्ध्वाधोलोकेषु यदुपभुक्तं तत्तद्भोगवासनादिभिर्हि कर्मक्षयेण मनुष्यलोकं प्राप्तानां तत्तदनुरूपेषु कर्मसु प्रवृत्तिर्भवति। एतस्मिन्नेव हि कर्माधिकारो नान्येषु लोकेषु। अतो मनुष्यलोके इत्युक्तम्।

Further, Hiraṇyagarbha and other individual beings conditioned by effects were described as branches. Among them, evildoers spread downward into animal and other wombs, while the meritorious spread upward into divine and other wombs; these are branches of the saṃsāra-tree. They grow according to the guṇas, the activities of sattva and the rest, as if watered. Their shoots are sense objects such as form, because they are connected with the subsidiary branches, the activities of the senses. Roots extend downward and, by the word ‘and,’ upward also. The principal root is the Lord alone; these secondary roots are the latent desires for particular enjoyments. Their function is to bind to karma in the human world: after enjoyment in higher or lower worlds, when karma is exhausted and beings return to the human world, the latent impressions of those enjoyments impel them toward corresponding actions. Only in the human world is there eligibility for karma, not in other worlds; therefore ‘in the human world’ is specified.

किंच -- न रूपमस्येति। इह संसारे स्थितैः प्राणिभिरस्य संसारवृक्षस्य तथोर्ध्वमूलत्वादिप्रकारेण रूपं नोपलभ्यते। न चान्तोऽवसानं? अपर्यन्तत्वात्। न चादिरनादित्वात्। नच संप्रतिष्ठा स्थितिः कथं तिष्ठतीति न चोपलभ्यते। यस्मादेवंभूतोऽयं संसारवृक्षो दुरुच्छेद्योऽनर्थकरश्च तस्मादेनं दृढेन वैराग्येण शस्त्रेण छित्त्वा तत्त्वज्ञाने यतेतेत्याह -- अश्वत्थमेनमिति सार्धेन। एनमश्वत्थं सुविरूढमूलमत्यन्तं बद्धमूलं सन्तमसङ्गः सङ्गराहित्यं अहंममतात्यागस्तेन दृढेन शस्त्रेण सम्यग्विचारेण छित्त्वा पृथक्कृत्य।

Further, beings situated in this saṃsāra do not perceive the form of the saṃsāra-tree as having its root above and so forth. They do not perceive its end because it has no boundary, nor its beginning because it is beginningless, nor its stable basis—how exactly it continues. Since this tree is difficult to cut and produces evil, He says that after cutting it with the strong weapon of dispassion one should strive for knowledge of reality. Cut apart this deeply and firmly rooted aśvattha with the strong weapon of non-attachment—freedom from association and abandonment of ‘I’ and ‘mine’—through proper discrimination.

तत इति। ततस्तस्य मूलभूतं तत्पदं वस्तु वैष्णवं पदं परिमार्गितव्यमन्वेष्टव्यम्। कीदृशम्। यस्मिन्गता यत्पदं प्राप्ताः सन्तो भूयो न निवर्तन्ति। नावर्तन्त इत्यर्थः। अन्वेषणप्रकारमाह। यत एषा पुराणी चिरंतनी संसारप्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता विस्तृता तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये शरणं व्रजामीत्येवमेकान्तभक्त्यान्वेष्टव्यमित्यर्थः।

Then its root-reality, that Vaiṣṇava state, is to be sought. What is it like? Those who reach that state do not return again. He explains how to seek it: ‘I take refuge in that very primal Person from whom this ancient, beginningless activity of saṃsāra has spread forth.’ Thus it is to be sought through exclusive devotion and surrender.

तत्प्राप्तौ साधनान्तराणि दर्शयन्नाह -- निर्मानेति। निर्गतौ मानमोहावहंकारमिथ्याभिनिवेशौ येभ्यस्ते? जितः पुत्रादिसङ्गरूपो दोषो यैस्ते? अध्यात्मे आत्मज्ञाने नित्याः परिनिष्ठिताः? विशेषेण निवृत्तः कामो येभ्यस्ते? सुखदुःखहेतुत्वात् सुखदुःखसंज्ञानि शीतोष्णादीनि द्वन्द्वानि तैर्विमुक्ताः? अतएवामूढाः निवृत्ताविद्याः सन्तस्तदव्ययं पदं वैष्णवं गच्छन्ति।

He gives additional means to attain it. Those from whom pride and delusion—egoism and false fixation—have departed; who have conquered the defect of attachment to sons and the like; who are constantly established in knowledge of the Self; whose desires have especially ceased; who are free from pairs such as heat and cold called pleasure and pain because they cause pleasure and pain; and who are therefore undeluded, their ignorance ended—such persons reach that imperishable Vaiṣṇava state.
तदेव गन्तव्यं पदं विशिनष्टि -- न तदिति। यत्पदं सूर्यादयो न प्रकाशयन्ति? यत्प्राप्य न निवर्तन्ते योगिनः? तद्धाम स्वरूपं परमं मम। अनेन सूर्यादिप्रकाशाविषयत्वेन जडत्वशीतोष्णादिदोषप्रसङ्गो निरस्तः।

He specifies that very state to be reached. The state that the sun and other lights do not illuminate, and having reached which yogins do not return, is My supreme abode, My very nature. By saying it is not an object illuminated by the sun and the rest, He excludes defects such as insentience, heat and cold.

ननु च त्वदीयं धाम प्राप्ताः सन्तो यदि न निवर्तन्ते तर्हिसति संपद्य न विदुः सति संपद्यामहे इत्यादिश्रुतेः सुषुप्तिप्रलयसमये त्वत्प्राप्तिः सर्वेषामस्तीति को नाम संसारी स्यादित्याशङ्क्य संसारिणं दर्शयति -- ममेति पञ्चभिः। ममैवांशो योऽयमविद्यया जीवभूतः सनातनः सर्वदा संसारित्वेन प्रसिद्धः असौ सुषुप्तिप्रलययोः प्रकृतौ लीनतया स्थितानि मनः षष्ठं येषां तानीन्द्रियाणि पुनर्जीवलोके संसारे भोगार्थमाकर्षति। एतच्च कर्मेन्द्रियाणां प्राणस्य चोपलक्षणार्थम्। अयं भावः -- सत्यं सुषुप्तिप्रलयोरपि मदंशत्वात्सर्वस्यापि जीवमात्रस्य मयि लयादस्त्येव मत्प्राप्तिः तथाप्यविद्ययावृतस्य सानुशयस्य सप्रकृतिके मयि लयो न तु शुद्धे। तदुक्तम् -- अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तयः सर्वाः प्रभवन्ति इत्यादिना। अतश्च पुनः संसाराय निर्गच्छन्नविद्वान् प्रकृतौ लीनतया स्थितानि स्वोपाधिभूतानीन्द्रियाण्याकर्षति। विदुषां तु शुद्धस्वरूपप्राप्तेर्नावृत्तिरिति।

An objection arises: if those who reach Your abode do not return, then according to scriptures such as ‘having merged in Being they do not know that they merge in Being,’ everyone attains You in deep sleep and dissolution; who then would remain in saṃsāra? He describes the saṃsāric individual in five verses. This eternal being, which is indeed a portion of Me but has become an individual soul through ignorance and is always known as transmigrating, again draws to itself in the world of living beings the senses that had remained dissolved in prakṛti during deep sleep and cosmic dissolution, with mind as the sixth, for the sake of experience. This also includes the organs of action and vital breath. The purport is: it is true that in sleep and dissolution every individual soul, being My portion, attains Me by dissolving in Me; but one covered by ignorance and carrying latent impressions dissolves into Me together with prakṛti, not into My pure nature. This was said in ‘From the unmanifest all manifestations arise.’ Therefore, emerging again for saṃsāra, the ignorant soul draws out the senses, its limiting adjuncts, which had dissolved in prakṛti. The knower, however, having attained the pure nature, does not return.

तान्याकृष्य किं करोतीत्यत्राह -- शरीरमिति। यदा शरीरान्तरं कर्मवशादवाप्नोति यतश्च शरीरादुत्क्रामति ईश्वरो देहादीनां स्वामी तदा पूर्वस्माच्छरीरादेतानि गृहीत्वा तच्छरीरान्तरं सम्यग्याति। शरीरे सत्यपीन्द्रियग्रहणे दृष्टान्तः। आशयात्स्वस्थानात्कुसुमादेः सकाशात् गन्धान्गन्धवतः सूक्ष्मानंशान्गृहीत्वा यथा वायुर्गच्छति तद्वत्।

What does it do after drawing them? When by force of karma it obtains another body and leaves the former body, the individual lord, master of the body and senses, takes these senses from the previous body and goes with them to the new body. The example illustrates taking the senses while the body still exists: just as wind takes subtle scent-bearing particles from their seat, such as a flower, and carries them away.
तान्येवेन्द्रियाणि दर्शयन्यदर्थं गृहीत्वा गच्छति तदाह -- श्रोत्रमिति। श्रोत्रादीनि बाह्येन्द्रियाणि मनश्चान्तःकरणमधिष्ठायाश्रित्य शब्दादीन्विषयानयं जीव उपभुङ्क्ते।
He names the senses and states why the soul takes them. Resorting to the external senses such as hearing and to mind, the internal organ, this individual soul experiences objects such as sound.

ननु च कार्यकारणसंघातव्यतिरेकेणैवंभूतमात्मानं सर्वेऽपि किं न पश्यन्ति तत्राह -- उत्क्रामन्तमिति। उत्क्रामन्तं देहाद्देहान्तरं गच्छन्तम्। तस्मिन्नेव देहे स्थितं वा विषयान्भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितमिन्द्रियादियुक्तं जीवं विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति नालोकयन्ति। ज्ञानमेव चक्षुर्येषां ते विवेकिनः पश्यन्ति।

Why does everyone not see such a Self as distinct from the aggregate of body and instruments? The deluded do not see the individual soul as it departs from one body to another, remains in the same body, or experiences objects while associated with the guṇas, senses and the rest. Those whose eye is knowledge—the discriminating—do see it.

दुर्ज्ञेयश्चायं यतो विवेकिष्वपि केचिदेव केचिन्न पश्यन्तीत्याह -- यतन्त इति। यतन्तः ध्यानादिभिः प्रयतमाना योगिनः केचिदेनमात्मानं आत्मनि देहेऽवस्थितं विविक्तं पश्यन्ति। शास्त्राभ्यासादिभिः प्रयत्नं कुर्वाणा अपि अकृतात्मानोऽविशुद्धचित्ताः अतएवाचेतसो मन्दमतय एनं न पश्यन्ति।

This Self is difficult to know, because even among discriminating persons only some see it. Some striving yogins, making effort through meditation and the like, see this distinct Self situated in the body. Others, though striving through scriptural study and the like, do not see it because they have not purified themselves, their minds are impure, and consequently they are unreflective and dull-minded.

तदेवंन तद्भासयते सूर्यः इत्यादिना पारमेश्वरं परं धामोक्तं? तत्प्राप्तानां चापुनरावृत्तिरुक्ता? तत्र च संसारिणोऽभावमाशङ्क्य संसारिस्वरूपं देहादिव्यतिरिक्तं दर्शितम्? इदानीं तदेव पारमेश्वरं रूपमनन्तशक्तित्वेन निरूपयति -- यदेत्यादिचतुर्भिः। आदित्यादिषु स्थितं यदनेकप्रकारं तेजो विश्वं प्रकाशयति तत्सर्वं तेजो मदीयमेव जानीहि।

Thus ‘the sun does not illumine it’ described the Supreme Lord’s highest abode and stated that those who attain it do not return. Anticipating the objection that this would leave no transmigrating souls, He then showed the transmigrating self as distinct from body and the rest. Now in four verses He describes that same supreme nature as possessing infinite power. Whatever many kinds of brilliance reside in the sun and other lights and illuminate the universe, know all that brilliance to be Mine alone.
किंच -- गामाविश्येति। गां पृथ्वीमोजसा बलेनाधिष्ठाय अहमेव चराचराणि भूतानि धारयामि? अहमेव रसमयः सोमो भूत्वा व्रीह्याद्यौषधीः सर्वाः संवर्धयामि।

Further, entering and presiding over the earth by My strength, I alone sustain all moving and unmoving beings; becoming Soma, full of nourishing essence, I alone cause all plants such as rice to grow.

किंच -- अहमिति। वैश्वानरो जाठरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहस्यान्तः प्रविश्य प्राणापानाभ्यां तदुद्दीपकाभ्यां सहितः प्राणिभिर्भुक्तं भक्ष्यं भोज्यं लेह्यं चोष्यं चेति चतुर्विधमन्नं पचामि। तत्र यद्दन्तैरवखण्ड्यावखण्ड्य भक्ष्यतेऽपूपादि तद्भक्ष्यम्। यत्तु केवलं जिह्वया विलोड्य निगीर्यते पायासादि तद्भोज्यम्। यत्तु जिह्वायां निक्षिप्य रसास्वादेन क्रमशो निगीर्यते द्रवीभूतं गुडादि तल्लेह्यम्। यत्तु दंष्ट्रादिभिर्निष्पीड्य रसांशं निगीर्यावशिष्टं त्यज्यत इक्षुदण्डादि तच्चोष्यमिति चतुर्विधभेदः।

Further, becoming Vaiśvānara, the digestive fire, I enter the bodies of living beings and, together with prāṇa and apāna which fan that fire, digest the four kinds of food eaten by them: what is chewed, swallowed, licked and sucked. Food such as cakes that is repeatedly broken by the teeth and eaten is ‘chewed.’ Food such as milk-rice that is moved by the tongue and swallowed is ‘swallowed.’ Liquefied food such as jaggery that is placed on the tongue, savored, and gradually swallowed is ‘licked.’ Food such as sugarcane that is pressed by the teeth and the like, whose juice is swallowed while the residue is discarded, is ‘sucked.’ Thus there are four kinds.

किंच -- सर्वस्येति। सर्वस्य प्राणिजातस्य हृदि सम्यगन्तर्यामिरूपेण प्रविष्टोऽहम्। अतश्च मत्त एव हेतोः प्राणिमात्रस्य पूर्वानुभूतार्थविषया स्मृतिर्भवति। ज्ञानं च विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगजं भवति। अपोहनं च तयोः प्रमोषो भवति। वेदैश्च सर्वैस्तत्तद्देवतादिरूपेणाहमेव वेद्यः। वेदान्तकृत्तत्संप्रदायप्रवर्तकश्च ज्ञानदो गुरुरहमित्यर्थः। वेदविदेव च वेदार्थविदहमेव।

Further, I have entered the heart of every living being completely as the inner controller. Therefore from Me alone arise memory of previously experienced objects, knowledge produced by contact of sense and object, and loss or removal of memory and knowledge. By all the Vedas I alone am to be known in the forms of the various deities and the rest. I am the maker of Vedānta, meaning the teacher who gives knowledge and establishes its tradition, and I alone truly know the Veda and its meaning.

इदानींतद्धाम परमं मम इति यदुक्तं तत्स्वकीयं सर्वोत्तमत्वं दर्शयति -- द्वाविमाविति त्रिभिः। क्षरश्चाक्षरश्चेति द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके प्रसिद्धौ। तावेवाह। तत्र क्षरः पुरुषो नाम सर्वाणि भूतानि ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तानि शरीराणि? अविवेकिलोकस्य शरीरेष्वेव पुरुषत्वप्रसिद्धेः। कूटः शिलाराशिः पर्वत इव देहेषु नश्यत्स्वपि निर्विकारतया तिष्ठतीति कूटस्थश्चेतनो भोक्ता। स तु अक्षरः पुरुष इत्युच्यते विवेकिभिः।

Now He shows His own supreme superiority referred to in ‘that is My supreme abode.’ Two persons are well known in the world: the perishable and the imperishable. The perishable ‘person’ means all bodies from Brahmā down to stationary beings, because undiscriminating people conventionally identify personhood with bodies. The conscious experiencer that remains changeless like a heap of stone or mountain even while bodies perish is ‘kūṭastha’ and is called the imperishable person by discriminating people.

यदर्थमेतौ लक्षितौ तमाह -- उत्तम इति। एताभ्यां क्षराक्षराभ्यामन्यो विलक्षणस्तूत्तमः पुरुषः। वैलक्षण्यमेवाह। परमश्चासावात्मेति चोदाहृत उक्तः श्रुतिभिः। आत्मत्वेन क्षरादचेतनाद्विलक्षणः परमत्वेनाक्षराच्चेतनाद्भोक्तुर्विलक्षण इत्यर्थः। परमात्मत्वमेव दर्शयति यो लोकत्रयमिति। य ईश्वर ईशनशीलः? अव्ययश्च निर्विकार एव सन् लोकत्रयं कृत्स्नमाविश्य बिभर्ति पालयति।

He now states the One for whose sake those two were defined. Distinct from both the perishable and the imperishable is the Supreme Person. Scripture calls Him the ‘Supreme Self.’ As Self He differs from the insentient perishable; as Supreme He differs from the conscious imperishable experiencer. He shows this Supreme-Self status: the Lord, who rules, while Himself imperishable and changeless, enters the entire three worlds and sustains and protects them.

एवंभूतं पुरुषोत्तमत्वमात्मनो नामनिर्वचनेन दर्शयति -- यस्मादिति। यस्मात्क्षरं जडवर्गमतिक्रान्तोऽहं नित्यमुक्तत्वात्? अक्षराच्चेतनवर्गादप्युत्तमश्च नियन्तृत्वात्? अतो लोके वेदे च पुरुषोत्तम इति प्रथितः प्रख्यातोऽस्मि। तथाच श्रुतिःस वा अयमात्मा सर्वस्य वशी सर्वस्येशानः सर्वस्याधिपतिः सर्वमिदं प्रशास्ति इत्यादिः।

He explains the name ‘Supreme Person’ to show His nature. Because I transcend the perishable class of insentient things through being eternally liberated, and am higher even than the imperishable class of conscious selves through being their ruler, I am celebrated in both world and Veda as Puruṣottama, the Supreme Person. Scripture says, ‘This Self is the controller of all, the ruler of all, the lord of all; He governs all this,’ and so on.
एवंभूतेश्वरस्याज्ञातुः फलमाह -- यो मामिति। एवमुक्तप्रकारेणासंमूढो निश्चितमतिः सन् यो मां पुरुषोत्तमं जानाति स सर्वभावेन सर्वप्रकारेण मामेव भजति ततः सर्ववित् सर्वज्ञो भवति।

He states the fruit for one who knows the Lord in this way. Whoever, free from delusion and firm in understanding, knows Me as the Supreme Person in the manner just taught worships Me alone with his whole being and in every way; therefore he becomes a knower of all, all-knowing in the relevant sense.

अध्यायार्थमुपसंहरति -- इतीति। इत्यनेन प्रकारेण गुह्यतमं अतिरहस्यं संपूर्णं शास्त्रमेव मयोक्तम् न पुनर्विंशतिश्लोकमध्यायमात्रम्। हे अनघ व्यसनशून्यः? अत एतन्मदुक्तं शास्त्रं बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान् सम्यग्ज्ञानी कृतकृत्यश्च स्याद्योऽपि कोऽपि। हे भारत? त्वं कृतकृत्योसीति किं वक्तव्यमिति भावः।

He concludes the chapter’s meaning. In this manner I have taught the most secret, exceedingly hidden, complete scripture—not merely a chapter of twenty verses. O sinless one, free from vice, whoever understands this teaching spoken by Me becomes intelligent, possessed of right knowledge, and one who has accomplished what must be done. O Bhārata, how much more need it be said that you will become fulfilled?
